comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C2-C5 regarding time-dependent forgetting in object recognition. Both evaluations rate these findings as SUPPORTED with robust behavioral evidence. Reviewers praised the robustness of behavioral effects, matching OpenEval's assessment of converging statistical evidence.

Perfect agreement on claims C6-C10 regarding engram reactivation mechanism. Both evaluations rate as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers explicitly endorsed the evidence for engram role in forgetting, consistent with OpenEval's assessment of robust statistical evidence for reactivation-based forgetting.

Perfect agreement on claims C11-C13 regarding morphological changes. Both evaluations rate as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers accepted spine density/volume findings without critique, matching OpenEval's assessment while acknowledging the limitation about reactivated vs non-reactivated cells.

Perfect agreement on claims C14-C17 regarding necessity of engram activity. Both evaluations rate as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers specifically praised the gain/loss of function approaches and appropriate controls, consistent with OpenEval's assessment of causal demonstration.

Perfect agreement on claims C18-C22 regarding sufficiency of engram activation. Both evaluations rate as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers explicitly endorsed the claim that forgotten engrams remain accessible, matching OpenEval's assessment while noting the sound logic of the approach.

Perfect agreement on claims C24-C29 regarding environmental enrichment effects. Both evaluations rate as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers praised the systematic testing approach, consistent with OpenEval's assessment while both acknowledge the complexity of interpreting enrichment effects.

Perfect agreement on claims C30-C33 regarding enrichment's cellular mechanism. Both evaluations rate as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers accepted the pattern of selective effects on engram reactivation without critique, matching OpenEval's assessment of robust statistical evidence.

Perfect agreement on claim C34 regarding neurogenesis markers. Both evaluations rate as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers treated this as an accepted supporting observation for enrichment validation, consistent with OpenEval's assessment as a positive control.

Strong agreement on claims C37-C44 regarding reminder effects (OpenEval includes C36 additionally). Both evaluations rate as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers praised systematic testing, matching OpenEval's assessment. OpenEval notes small sample size concern not mentioned by peer reviewers.

Disagreement on claims C45-C49 regarding context-only exposure. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to alternative interpretation (renewed interest vs true forgetting), while peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED and praised the 'clever' behavioral methods. This represents a substantive difference in interpretation.

Disagreement on claims C50-C53 regarding engram activity requirement for experience-dependent forgetting. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN (dependent on uncertain interpretation of C45-C49), while peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED and praised the approach. OpenEval's uncertainty cascades from the context-only experiment interpretation.

Perfect agreement on claims C56-C61 regarding Rac1 inhibition effects. Both evaluations rate as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers praised the variety of methods, matching OpenEval's assessment of robust statistical evidence. OpenEval notes a potential reporting error in C61 not mentioned by peer reviewers.

Perfect agreement on claims C62-C67 regarding Rac1 activation effects. Both evaluations rate as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers accepted the bidirectional manipulation as strong evidence, consistent with OpenEval's assessment of robust statistical evidence and consistent mechanistic pattern.

Perfect agreement on claims C68-C69 regarding Rac1 mechanistic synthesis. Both evaluations rate as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers accepted the interpretive conclusions as reasonable syntheses, matching OpenEval's assessment while noting the adaptive forgetting speculation requires further testing.

Strong agreement on claims C70-C82 regarding computational modeling (OpenEval includes C83 additionally). Both evaluations rate as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers praised the novel application of Rescorla-Wagner model, matching OpenEval's assessment of model validation. Both note the model's relative simplicity.

Partial overlap on claim C83. Both evaluations rate as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers accepted the speculative extension about learning rate modulation, consistent with OpenEval's broader assessment of the computational framework's ability to integrate experimental findings.

Partial overlap on claims C1, C85-C93 (OpenEval) vs C84, C93, C147 (peer). Both evaluations rate as SUPPORTED. Both endorse the conceptual framework and main conclusions. OpenEval focuses on literature framing and hypothesis articulation, while peer reviewers emphasize the importance and convincing nature of the overall work.

OpenEval evaluated claims C94-C103 regarding alternative explanations and ruling out encoding/consolidation failures as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though these conceptual points underlie peer acceptance of the retrieval-based forgetting framework.

OpenEval evaluated claims C104-C113 regarding enrichment literature context as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found. These claims situate findings within established literature but were not explicitly evaluated by peer reviewers.

Partial overlap on claims C114-C121 (OpenEval) vs C117-C119 (peer). Both evaluations rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval provides broader assessment of theoretical integration, while peer reviewers focus on learning rate interpretations and pathological extremes as reasonable extensions.

OpenEval evaluated claims C122-C128 regarding Rescorla-Wagner theoretical framework as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though peer reviewers praised the modeling approach in R15 which encompasses these theoretical foundations.

OpenEval evaluated claims C129-C138 regarding Rac1 literature context as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found. These claims contextualize Rac1 findings within broader neuroscience but were not explicitly evaluated separately by peer reviewers.

OpenEval evaluated claims C139-C143 regarding extinction and memory competition context as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though Reviewer 2 noted conceptual similarity to extinction in their general comments.

Partial overlap on claims C144-C147 (OpenEval) vs C84, C93, C147 (peer). Both evaluations rate as SUPPORTED. Both endorse the main conclusion that forgetting is adaptive learning. OpenEval provides more detailed assessment of the adaptive vs pathological framing, while peer reviewers emphasize the overall importance and convincing evidence.
